## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Kukkuṭajātaka* (Ja 209), rendered in English as "The Old Chook" by Bhikkhu Sujato, is a canonical narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in its opening blurb, the Buddha recounted this story while residing at Jetavana regarding a monk who was one of the fellow-students of Venerable Sāriputta, the Captain of the Faith (*dhammasenāpati*) [SuttaCentral]. The story opens with the verse phrase, "Trees a many have I seen" [SuttaCentral].

Regarding parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral records a full parallel preserved in the Sanskrit Mahāvastu of the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda tradition (Mvu 59, "The Jātaka of the Bird (2)") [SuttaCentral]. Machine alignment by DharmaNexus detects no internal Pali text reuse and finds no cross-language matches reaching the threshold score of 10 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral additionally registers four translations across four modern languages [SuttaCentral].

While multiple occurrences of the title *Kukkuṭajātaka* appear across Buddhist literature and art, other references in the reference dossier concern separate works or homonymous entities. These include two distinct Jātakas bearing the identical title—Ja 383 (concerning a cock and a cat) and Ja 448 (concerning a cock and a hawk)—as well as the *Akālarāvi-kukkuṭa-jātaka* (Ja 119), the Kukkuṭārāma monastery, the Kaukkutika school, and figures named Kukkuṭa or Kukkuṭamitta in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*. None of the secondary passages in the provided dossier directly address Ja 209.
